target.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Windows file-transfer policy edge case where home-relative globs written with Windows path separators, such as `~\Downloads\**`, were treated as literal glob text instead of being expanded to the user's home directory.

The file-transfer policy already supports home-relative patterns through `~/...` and bare `~`. However, Windows users naturally tend to write local paths with backslashes, and `~\...` looked like the Windows equivalent of `~/...` in configuration. Before this change, that form was not recognized by `expandTilde()`, so the policy matcher received a pattern that still began with a literal `~\` prefix.

That created two confusing outcomes:

- `allowReadPaths` or `allowWritePaths` entries such as `~\Downloads\**` could fail to match files that are actually under the user's home directory.
- `denyPaths` entries such as `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` could fail to enforce the intended hard-deny rule, because the deny glob never resolved to the real home-directory path.

In practice, a Windows operator could configure a policy that appears to allow or deny the correct local folder, while file-transfer policy evaluation behaves differently because only the forward-slash tilde form was expanded.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change extends the existing tilde expansion helper to recognize `~\` as the Windows-style equivalent of `~/`.

The fix is intentionally small and stays inside the shared policy normalization path. `normalizeGlobs()` is already used before matching `allowReadPaths`, `allowWritePaths`, and `denyPaths`, so updating `expandTilde()` gives all three policy surfaces the same home-relative behavior without duplicating logic or changing the matcher itself.

Existing behavior is preserved for:

- `~/...` home-relative globs
- bare `~`
- absolute paths
- normal minimatch semantics
- Windows path separator normalization during matching
- deny-before-allow policy precedence

The change only makes a previously unexpanded Windows-style home prefix behave like the already-supported POSIX-style home prefix. This keeps the policy model consistent while avoiding a broader rewrite of path handling or glob evaluation.

## User Impact

Windows users can now configure file-transfer policy globs using familiar Windows separators, for example:

```text
~\Downloads\**
```

and have them resolve against the same home directory target as:

```text
~/Downloads/**
```

This also makes Windows-style hard-deny rules behave as configured, for example `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` now denies matching files under the user's Downloads directory instead of remaining a non-matching literal pattern.

## Live Windows Behavior Proof

Redacted live proof was run on Windows against the production file-transfer policy evaluator, not a mock. The proof uses the same `evaluateFilePolicy()` path that file-transfer node-invoke policy calls before file fetch/list/write execution.

```text
Windows file-transfer policy live proof
platform=win32
node=v24.15.0
home=<USER_HOME>
config.allowReadPaths=["~\\Downloads\\**"]
config.denyPaths=["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
case=ALLOW Windows-style home glob
path=<USER_HOME>\Downloads\shot.png
decision=matched-allow
ok=true
case=DENY Windows-style hard-deny glob
path=<USER_HOME>\Downloads\key.pem
decision=POLICY_DENIED
ok=false
```

This proves both requested behaviors from a real Windows run:

- `~\Downloads\**` resolves as a home-relative allow glob and permits a matching non-denied file.
- `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` resolves as a home-relative deny glob and still wins over the broader allow rule.

## Compatibility / Security-Boundary Note

This PR intentionally changes how existing file-transfer policy strings beginning with `~\` are interpreted. Before this fix, those entries were effectively literal non-matches; after this fix, they become active home-relative policy globs.

That is the intended Windows policy interpretation: a stored config entry such as `~\Downloads\**` already expresses operator intent to target the user's Downloads directory. The change does not add a new wildcard class or bypass deny precedence; it only makes the Windows-style home prefix behave like the already-supported `~/` home prefix.

Because this is a file-access policy surface, the PR includes both allow and hard-deny proof. The deny proof demonstrates that broad Windows-style allow rules still remain constrained by `denyPaths` after expansion.

## Evidence

Live proof command:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node --import tsx --input-type=module <redacted inline policy proof script>
```

Focused validation passed using the repository Vitest runner with hydrated dependencies:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       32 passed (32)
```

Diff hygiene also passed for the touched files:

```text
git diff --check -- extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.ts extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts
```

The added regression cases cover both directions:

```text
allowReadPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**"]
path: <home>/Downloads/shot.png
result: matched allow
```

```text
denyPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
path: <home>/Downloads/key.pem
result: POLICY_DENIED
```

target.title: Add reset family carryover summaries
target.body:
## Behavior or issue addressed

Depends on #90239.

When a session has been reset/rotated, the active transcript can be clean while the previous reset archive still contains the latest compaction summary. The next embedded-agent prompt therefore starts without the carryover context unless the model/tool explicitly asks for family history.

This change reuses the session-family transcript resolver from #90239 and injects the latest reset-archive compaction summary into embedded-agent prompt context before the LLM boundary, but only when the active context does not already contain a compaction summary.

## Fix

- Move the #90239 family/reset transcript target resolver into a shared gateway helper.
- Keep `chat.history(includeFamily)` on the shared resolver.
- Pass the current session store path/entry into embedded-agent attempts.
- Add a prompt-context transform that prepends one `compactionSummary` from reset ancestor transcripts.
- Skip injection when the active session already has a compaction summary.
- Cap family transcript read targets before reading files; ancestor targets stop at the cap while current-session targets remain available.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main` and preserved the newer transcript-reader seam plus same-session reset fallback.

## Real behavior proof

**Current head proven:** `ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c`.

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A reset/rotated logical session should read bounded reset-family history through the shared resolver, keep current reset archive plus current active transcript available inside the cap, preserve the newest eligible ancestors even when an older retained ancestor has many reset-topic archives, and inject exactly one reset-family compaction summary before the embedded-agent LLM boundary.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on this PR branch at `/home/clever/.openclaw/workspace/github/openclaw`, using current branch TypeScript modules and temporary on-disk session stores/transcripts under `/tmp/openclaw-family-proof-ba74ecd54e-*`. No private channel, endpoint, phone, prompt, auth, or user transcript data was used.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c

$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'TS'

# - ./src/gateway/session-history-family.ts
# - ./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-family-carryover.ts
# It created a temporary sessions.json, 35 ancestor transcripts,
# 35 owned reset-topic archives for ancestor 05, one current reset archive,
# and one current active transcript. It called the real family target resolver,
# real carryover resolver, installed the prompt transform, applied the transform
# twice, printed the observed result, and removed temp files.
TS
{
  "head": "ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c",
  "targetCount": 32,
  "firstTargets": [
    "ancestor-proof-05:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-05.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-06:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-06.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-07:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-07.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-08:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-08.jsonl"
  ],
  "lastTargets": [
    "ancestor-proof-33:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-33.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-34:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-34.jsonl",
    "current-proof-session:reset-archive:current-proof-session.jsonl.reset.2026-06-04T00-04-00.000Z",

  ],
  "currentResetTargetPresent": true,
  "currentActiveLast": true,
  "ancestor04Present": false,
  "ancestor34Present": true,
  "archiveHeavyTopicTargetCount": 0,
  "carryoverSummary": "Exact-head ba74ecd54e carryover 34",
  "carryoverTokensBefore": 2034,
  "promptRolesBeforeLlm": ["compactionSummary", "user"],
  "compactionSummaryCount": 1,
  "idempotentRoles": ["compactionSummary", "user"]
}
```

**Evidence after fix:**

- The shared resolver returned 32 targets and kept both current reset archive and current active transcript inside the cap.
- The current active transcript was ordered last for final history trimming.
- The old over-cap ancestor was not read: `ancestor04Present` is false.
- The newest eligible ancestor survived even though older retained ancestor 05 had 35 owned reset-topic archives: `ancestor34Present` is true and `archiveHeavyTopicTargetCount` is 0.

**What was not tested:** Full live Telegram/Slack/Discord end-to-end reset turn was not run locally; the proof exercises the real resolver and embedded carryover path against on-disk OpenClaw-like session artifacts.
## Current head addendum: `f59176b8ac`

ClawSweeper's exact-head proof request is addressed on current head `f59176b8acbb9847ab4c69c09ad4539cde66b9d0`.

The carryover prompt injection is now default-off and requires explicit `agents.defaults.experimental.sessionFamilyCarryover: true`. The proof below uses current-branch modules, temporary on-disk reset-family transcript files, the real reset-family carryover resolver, and the real transform installer/gate.

```text
f59176b8acbb9847ab4c69c09ad4539cde66b9d0

# and removes temp files.
TS

}
```

Observed result after fix:

## Behavior or issue addressed

Depends on #90239.

When a session has been reset/rotated, the active transcript can be clean while the previous reset archive still contains the latest compaction summary. The next embedded-agent prompt therefore starts without the carryover context unless the model/tool explicitly asks for family history.

This change reuses the session-family transcript resolver from #90239 and injects the latest reset-archive compaction summary into embedded-agent prompt context before the LLM boundary, but only when the active context does not already contain a compaction summary.

## Fix

- Move the #90239 family/reset transcript target resolver into a shared gateway helper.
- Keep `chat.history(includeFamily)` on the shared resolver.
- Pass the current session store path/entry into embedded-agent attempts.
- Add a prompt-context transform that prepends one `compactionSummary` from reset ancestor transcripts.
- Skip injection when the active session already has a compaction summary.
- Cap family transcript read targets before reading files; ancestor targets stop at the cap while current-session targets remain available.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main` and preserved the newer transcript-reader seam plus same-session reset fallback.
